title: Influence matrix: integrate deployment regime, cost & latency into RICE-like prioritization
creator: Anika Bose
description: We need a practical, explainable prioritization artifact ("Influence Matrix") that extends classic RICE to account for deployment regime constraints (hosted, dedicated, private), per-token cost delta, and latency SLO penalties. Goal: enable PMs to rank initiatives not just by user reach and confidence but by the end-to-end production economics and rollout risk across Redwood's three deployment modes. Deliverable: a spreadsheet + scoring library + short how-to doc that teams can apply to candidate roadmap items.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A reproducible scoring spreadsheet that takes as inputs: Reach, Effort, Confidence, Deployment Regime weights, Estimated cost delta (per 1M tokens), Latency SLO penalty factor, Rollout complexity; produces a ranked list.
2) A lightweight python scoring library (pip or internal) with unit tests covering edge cases (zero-cost, high-latency penalty).
3) Internal guide (Confluence) with worked examples using 3 historical initiatives and one customer scenario.
4) Sign-off from Eng leads on model assumptions and from Growth PM on reach modeling.
steps: 1) Prototype influence functions for (a) regime-adjusted effort multiplier and (b) latency penalty curve (sigmoid-shaped beyond SLO).
2) Map cost signals: baseline hosted per-token vs dedicated reservation delta vs private ops delta (use telemetry and pricing models in console).
3) Build spreadsheet prototype and run against last 6 quarters of roadmap candidates (sanitized).
4) Implement scoring lib + unit tests and example CLI to score a CSV of candidate initiatives.
5) Write Confluence guide and short video (5min) for PMs.
6) Schedule review with Eng infra leads & Growth to validate assumptions and determine rollout policy recommendations.
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped as an MVP: we want a defensible, reproducible ranking that can be iterated, not a perfect econometric model. The Influence Matrix decouples 'value' from 'operational fit' so teams can see both a base priority and the deployment friction score.
open_questions: Q1: How do we normalize Reach across PLG usage vs enterprise committed seats? (proposal: segment and apply cohort multipliers)
Q2: Should Private deployments carry a fixed ops-surcharge or be modeled as uncertain (probabilistic) cost? (proposal: MVP uses fixed percentage, move to probabilistic later)
Q3: Where do we get latency penalty curves per model (LLM family)? (action: ask Applied ML for typical p95->p99 degradation impact)
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decided to keep RICE as the base but add two orthogonal axes: 'Deployment Friction' (0-10) and 'Operational Cost Delta' in $/1M tokens.
Trade-off: a single combined score is more actionable but hides deployment-specific blockers. We will publish both a combined rank and per-regime breakdown (hosted/dedicated/private).

Decision: Latency penalty will use a piecewise function: no penalty <= SLO; linear penalty for SLO->1.5x; exponential beyond 1.5x. Rationale: encourages solutions within SLO while strongly de-prioritizing options that would cause large regressions.
example_scoring: Example A (hosted chat reranking): Reach=80k DAU, Effort=5pts, Confidence=0.6, CostDelta=$200/1M tokens, Deployment friction=2 => InfluenceScore(base)= (Reach*Confidence)/Effort = 9600; RegimeFactor(hosted)=0.95; LatencyPenalty=1.0 => FinalScore=9120

Example B (private on-prem model tuning): Reach=3 enterprise customers, Effort=13pts, Confidence=0.5, CostDelta=$1200/1M tokens, Deployment friction=8 => Base= (Reach*Confidence)/Effort = 0.115; RegimeFactor(private)=0.5; LatencyPenalty=1.4 => FinalScore=0.0805 (ranks very low)
Note: examples are illustrative; final spreadsheet will use normalized Reach units (score 0-100) so combined ranks are comparable across scales.
